feature_request.title: OTA software updates
feature_request.description: I want the bench's ECUs to take software updates over the air the way a production vehicle does: signed images, safe to interrupt, only when the vehicle is in a fit state, with a record of what was installed. Find what the bench already does and what is missing.
feature_request.motivation: Pilot 1 of the product development and test tool. The bench already has a large part of this (P4), so the tool's inventory can be checked against a feature whose real state is known.

constraints.parts_owned_note: See config/hardware.json. Relay and sniffer parts were ordered on 2026-10-08.

Use measured values as the baseline: bus load at most the observed 1.11 % on the 500 kbit/s CAN bus, and a commit wait of 3.5 s. The update path protects a safety controller, so a failed or interrupted update must never leave unverified code running (hazard H9 / SG9). No standard integrity level is claimed.

items.title: Draft the UPD-xx update requirement family
items.detail: Cover what runs where, a record of every update and a compatibility check, as reference only with no compliance claim. This closes the missing requirement for per-board update records.

items.title: Draft the image signing requirement
items.detail: State that the public key is on the board, the private key is never on a board, and keys can be rotated. This replaces the HMAC demo key with ECDSA P-256 verify.

items.title: Draft gateway flashing and CAN interface requirements
items.detail: Specify the UDS programming sequence, block counter, interruption handling and bus-load limit. Also specify the request and response ids, message format and error responses of the gateway CAN interface.

items.title: Decide scope of multi-board campaign and state its behaviour
items.detail: The owner decision on fault cases (supply sag, one ECU failing after another committed) is still open. Decide which cases are in scope and state the expected behaviour and activation rule.

items.title: Draft the update precondition requirement
items.detail: Define the supply floor, the vehicle state and the refusal reason, so an update starts only when the supply is high enough to finish.

items.title: Write the baseline budget requirements
items.detail: Record bus load at most the observed 1.11 % on the 500 kbit/s CAN bus and a commit wait of 3.5 s. Flash and RAM budgets wait for the flash-use conflict to be resolved.

items.title: Draft the release evidence requirement
items.detail: Require test reports, a manifest and a release verdict for each release.

items.title: Allocate the gateway role and register programming CAN ids
items.detail: Give board A the gateway role and register the programming use of the reserved UDS ids (0x7E2/0x7EA, 0x7E3/0x7EB, 0x7DF). Add any extra ids to config/can_ids.json and the DBC, and set flash-time and bus-load budgets.

items.title: Add a vehicle-state / supply message to the CAN registry
items.detail: Add the message to the CAN registry and the DBC so the update path can read vehicle state and supply.

items.title: Build the 12 V supply and battery model
items.detail: Model state of charge, sag under load, brown-out threshold and sag during erase and write. Include the sag for the campaign case only if the owner keeps it in scope.

items.title: Resolve and fit supply-voltage sensing input
items.detail: This needs a divider and filter on an ADC pin, but the scope says no new part is bought. The owner must accept the purchase and change the scope, or find another way.

items.title: Extend the manifest with update records and set manifest
items.detail: Add a per-update record next to the installed version per board. Add a set manifest, a compatibility check and the chosen activation rule for campaigns.

items.title: Implement ECDSA P-256 verify and PC signing
items.detail: Implement verify in software on board B and signing on the PC. Measure verify time and flash/RAM first.

items.title: Implement the UDS programming server and gateway client
items.detail: Build the server on board B and the gateway client on board A in the portable core, following the specified CAN interface.

items.title: Add the supply and vehicle-state precondition to the update path
items.detail: Today the only check is 'scenario running = BUSY'. Refuse the update below the supply floor with a reason.

items.title: Implement ISO-TP multi-frame transport
items.detail: Add segmentation, flow control, block size and STmin in the portable core for host and target, with conformance cases. Today the responder accepts single frames only, which cannot carry image blocks.

items.title: Fit relay, adapter and data-only lead once parts arrive
items.detail: The relay, adapter and screw terminal are owned but not fitted. Wait for the ordered USB breakouts, then fit them. The owner confirms arrival in config/hardware.json. List which work depends on the ordered parts, including any hardware needed for the budget checks.

items.title: Extend the REL matrix for signing
items.detail: Add cases for a wrong public key, a signature by a key not on the board and a tampered signature.

items.title: Add REL cases for the CAN flashing path
items.detail: Cover a wrong block counter, interruption at every block and reset in each state.

items.title: Add fault tests for the kept campaign cases
items.detail: Test one board failing after another has committed, for the cases the owner keeps.

items.title: Add REL cases for the supply floor
items.detail: Check that the update is refused below the supply floor and accepted above it.

items.title: Run the physical supply-cut test of board B
items.detail: Cut the supply with the relay and the data-only USB lead on the bench, not only emulated. This closes the P4 open item.

items.title: Add a sag-during-write test and measure brown-out threshold
items.detail: Test a supply sag during erase and write against the 12 V model. Measure the board's brown-out threshold on the bench.

items.title: Record the build and cppcheck results as a repeatable check
items.detail: Build the portable C++17 core with warnings as errors and run cppcheck. The MISRA C++:2023 subset is a reference only, with no compliance claim.

items.title: Check bus load and commit wait in the OTA runs
items.detail: Compare the measured bus load and commit wait against the 1.11 % and 3.5 s baselines.

functions.name: UDS programming client and campaign sequencer (gateway)
functions.rationale: N06 has Board A flash board B over CAN with a UDS programming sequence. Board A is the gateway, so the client and campaign sequencer sit there (gaps G-N06-architecture, G-N06-software).

functions.name: UDS programming server: 0x10, 0x27, 0x31, 0x34, 0x36, 0x37, 0x11
functions.rationale: Board B is the flashed target. The UDS services 0x10, 0x27, 0x31, 0x34, 0x36, 0x37 and 0x11 are the server side of the sequence, so they run on board B.

functions.name: ISO-TP multi-frame transport, client side
functions.rationale: N20 needs ISO-TP multi-frame transport on the diagnostic CAN interface. Board A sends the programming data as client, so segmentation and flow control sit here (G-N20-software missing).

functions.name: ISO-TP multi-frame transport, server side
functions.rationale: Board B receives the image blocks over ISO-TP and returns flow control, so the server side sits on the flashed target (G-N20-software missing).

functions.name: Image signature verify: ECDSA P-256 over the image hash, public key only on the board
functions.rationale: N05 requires the public key only on the board, so board B verifies the ECDSA P-256 signature over the image hash before it trusts the image. The private key never goes on a board.

functions.name: Image signing and campaign manifest builder (private key stays on the PC)
functions.rationale: N05 keeps the private key off the boards, so signing and the N08 campaign manifest are built on bench-pc (G-N05-software and G-N08-software are missing).

functions.name: Campaign rule: stage all, activate all, confirm all, roll back all together
functions.rationale: D-01b sets all-or-nothing activation across the campaign. Board A is the gateway that sees every board, so the rule sits there (G-N08-software missing).

functions.name: Per-board update record: version that runs, result, time
functions.rationale: N04 asks for a per-board record of the version that runs. The PC is the bench side and can keep the record. Whether storage is on the PC is not stated in the digest (G-N04-software missing).

functions.name: Update precondition on the target: supply floor, scenario idle
functions.rationale: N09 says the board reads the supply voltage before an update starts, so board B holds the supply floor and scenario-idle check on the target (G-N09-architecture, G-N09-software missing).

functions.name: Update precondition on the gateway: vehicle state and supply seen on the bus
functions.rationale: N09 also covers the vehicle state. Board A sees VEH_SupplyState on the bus, so the gateway gates the campaign start on it (G-N09-architecture missing).

functions.name: Supply-voltage sensing: divider to an ADC1 pin
functions.rationale: Board B reads its own supply voltage. D-02 allows a divider as one new BOM line, and the digest places it on an ADC1 pin of board B.

functions.name: Supply and vehicle-state source (VEH_SupplyState from the plant)
functions.rationale: The supply and vehicle state come from the plant model, which runs on the PC. It publishes VEH_SupplyState, which is a proposed message in the digest.

functions.name: Update status reporting to the bench (BUS_UpdateStatus)
functions.rationale: N17 asks for the gateway interface to the bench. Board A is the gateway, so it reports BUS_UpdateStatus to the PC (G-N17-architecture and G-N17-software are partial).

functions.name: Supply / battery plant model with sag, brown-out and supply cut
functions.rationale: D-01a puts supply sag in scope, modelled in the plant. N12 asks for sag, brown-out and supply cut. The plant model runs on the PC.

functions.name: Supply cut by relay (existing relay output on board A)
functions.rationale: N11 asks for a physical cut of board B's supply. The digest says the relay output already exists on board A, so the cut is triggered from there.

functions.name: Budget checks in the OTA runs: bus load, commit wait, flash time
functions.rationale: N15 sets timing and resource budgets, and the numbers come from code. The PC runs the OTA runs, so it checks bus load, commit wait and flash time there.

functions.name: Update record store and release evidence export
functions.rationale: N04 needs a per-board update record and N18 needs evidence per release. AF-08 holds the record. The digest does not say where it is stored, so that is unknown.

computations.title: Length of one classic CAN frame with 8 data bytes

inputs.name: N
inputs.source: ISO-TP frames are padded to 8 bytes

steps: nominal = 47 + 8 x 8 = 111 bits
stuffing = floor((34 + 8 x 8 - 1) / 4) = floor(97 / 4) = 24 bits
worst case = 111 + 24 = 135 bits = 270 us at 500 kbit/s

computations.title: Bus bits to move one 1024-byte TransferData block (ISO-TP)
computations.method: frames = 1 first + ceil((L - 6) / 7) consecutive + 1 flow control + 1 response; bits = frames x frame length

inputs.name: L (block length incl. SID and counter)
flow control
inputs.source: proposal: one flow-control frame per block

steps: data per block = 1024 - 2 (SID 0x36 + block counter) = 1022 bytes
consecutive frames = ceil((1024 - 6) / 7) = ceil(1018 / 7) = 146
bits (worst case) = 149 x 135 = 20115; bits (nominal) = 149 x 111 = 16539

computations.title: Time to move the board B image over CAN at stated bus shares
computations.method: total worst-case bits / (bit rate x bus share); the bus is the limit, the flash side is C4

inputs.name: observed max bus load
inputs.source: inventory CAN-BUS (max of the can/hil result files)

inputs.name: bus-share caps tried
inputs.source: proposal: the scope names no cap for programming traffic

steps: image = 1031920 bytes (hil/build/fw_b/SafetyNode.ino.bin, measured; the board B image is the '1 MB-class' image)
total bits (worst case) = 1010 x 20115 = 20316150

the whole bus (lower bound, not usable)

computations.method: typical SPI NOR figures; NOT measured on this board. T6 replaces it with the timing of the existing OTA matrix on the real board.

write = 1007.7 KiB / 100 KiB/s = 10.1 s

steps: existing traffic (max observed in the can/hil result files) = 1.11 %

computations.title: Flash headroom of board B for ISO-TP + UDS programming + ECDSA verify (ESTIMATE)
computations.method: measured image and slot (calculation) minus size classes of the added code (estimate: typical object sizes at -Os, unmeasured). The ECDSA figure has the widest range because the repo cannot say whether the TLS stack already links mbedTLS ecp/ecdsa. Replace by a build in T6.
steps: app slot = 1310720 bytes (1280 KiB); image now = 1031920 bytes = 78.7 % (measured; the 26 % in ssc_ota.h is a stale comment, inventory conflict flash.safetynode_use)
headroom = 1310720 - 1031920 = 278800 bytes = 272.3 KiB (21.3 % of the slot)
+ ISO-TP transport (FF/CF/FC, timers, buffers): 3 to 6 KiB
+ UDS programming server (0x10/0x27/0x31/0x34/0x36/0x37/0x11, NRCs, state machine): 6 to 12 KiB
+ campaign states: activate, trial, commit-pending, confirm, rollback: 3 to 8 KiB
+ ECDSA P-256 verify + ASN.1/pk glue (mbedTLS); low = ecp/ecdsa objects already linked by the TLS stack, high = linked fresh: 0 to 80 KiB
+ public key, manifest parsing, precondition check: 1 to 3 KiB
added code = 13 KiB (low) to 109 KiB (high); with a 25 % margin on the high figure = 136.25 KiB
image after = 1007.7 + 13 = 1020.7 KiB (low) to 1144.0 KiB (high + margin); slot = 1280 KiB
remaining headroom = 272.3 - 136.25 = 136.0 KiB (high case) = 10.6 % of the slot
verdict rule: does_not_fit if high+margin > headroom; tight if > 75% of the headroom; else fits_by_estimate -> fits_by_estimate

computations.method: measured image and slot minus a size class for UDS client + ISO-TP + campaign sequencer (10 to 25 KiB, unmeasured)
steps: headroom = 956.3 KiB; added 10 to 25 KiB (+25 %)
fits_by_estimate = True

computations.method: static RAM from the map file (measured) plus buffer and working-memory sizes (estimate)
steps: static RAM now = 53954 bytes = 15.8 % of 341760
+ ISO-TP receive buffer (one 1024-byte block) + transmit buffer: 2 to 2.5 KiB
+ CAN frame queue: 0.5 to 1 KiB
+ ECDSA verify working memory (heap): 3 to 8 KiB

computations.title: WCET and cycle impact on board B (ESTIMATE)
computations.method: frame arrival spacing is a calculation; the handler time and the ECDSA time are budgets and estimates, not measurements
steps: back-to-back consecutive frames arrive every 270 us at worst (C1)
handler budget 100 us per frame = 37 % of one core while a block streams

sequence.service: reads VEH_SupplyState; 0x22 0xF195 on each target; UDS 0x3E
sequence.action: Check supply above the floor, vehicle state parked, no scenario running on any target, every image newer than the installed version.
sequence.check: supply_mv >= floor and vehicle_state == parked and every target answers
sequence.on_failure: Do not start. Report the refusal reason on BUS_UpdateStatus. Nothing was changed.
sequence.detail: Before the start, board A checks the vehicle state and supply seen on the bus (AF-10). Board B checks its own supply floor and scenario idle (AF-09). Both must pass. The threshold values are not in the digest and must come from code.

sequence.action: Open the programming session on every target board of the campaign.
sequence.on_failure: Close all sessions (0x10 0x01). Nothing was changed.

sequence.action: Unlock programming on each target. Key scheme is an owner decision (R8).
sequence.check: positive response 0x67; wrong key gives NRC 0x35, repeated wrong keys lock out
sequence.on_failure: Close all sessions. Nothing was changed.

sequence.action: Erase only the inactive slot of each target.
sequence.check: 0x71 with status ok; NRC 0x78 while pending
sequence.on_failure: Abort the campaign: the running slot was never touched.

sequence.service: 0x34, then 0x36 with block counter 1.. (1022 data bytes), then 0x37
sequence.action: Send the image block by block over ISO-TP; the server writes each block and counts.
sequence.check: block counter matches; NRC 0x73 on a wrong counter; a repeated block is idempotent (resume by offset)
sequence.on_failure: Abort the campaign; every target keeps its running slot.

sequence.action: Verify SHA-256, the ECDSA signature, the version (anti-downgrade) and the manifest set on every target.
sequence.check: all targets report ok before ANY target is activated
sequence.on_failure: Abort the campaign; nothing is activated.

sequence.action: Switch the boot slot on all targets together, then reset them.
sequence.check: every target reboots into the new slot in state TRIAL

sequence.service: reads 0x22 0xF195 and its own health check
sequence.action: Each target proves the new image healthy within the trial time; a reset during the trial returns it to the old slot by itself.
sequence.check: version read equals the manifest and the health check passes
sequence.on_failure: That target rolls itself back; the gateway then rolls all others back (0x0203).

sequence.action: Each target enters commit-pending (new slot is the boot slot, old slot is KEPT). Only when every target is commit-pending the gateway confirms the campaign; then old slots may be released and the anti-downgrade counter moves.
sequence.check: all targets commit-pending, then all confirmed
sequence.on_failure: If one target fails after others are commit-pending: 0x0203 on every target returns all to the old slot. Needs anti-downgrade to allow an authorised campaign rollback (R6).
sequence.detail: D-01b says all boards in the campaign roll back together if one fails after another has committed (AF-07). Power-loss safety at each commit write is proven by REL-11 and REL-12 (N10). The digest does not give the commit steps.

sequence.action: Return every target of the campaign to its previous slot and confirm by version read.
sequence.check: every target reports the old version
sequence.on_failure: A target that does not answer is reported as a campaign failure; its own trial logic returns it to the old slot at the next reset.

multi_board_rule.source: owner decision 2026-10-16 (decisions.json D-01b); a bench design choice, not shown to be production practice (docs/OTA_PRODUCTION_REFERENCE.md)
stages: stage all images on all targets and verify them
each target proves a trial boot
every target commit-pending, then the campaign is confirmed together
multi_board_rule.failure_rule: A failure at any point before confirmation, including one board failing after another has reached commit-pending, returns EVERY board of the campaign to the previous slot.

risks.text: Adding ISO-TP, UDS programming and ECDSA verify to board B FITS BY ESTIMATE: headroom 272.3 KiB, added 13 to 109 KiB (136.2 KiB with margin), 136.0 KiB left in the worst case. The additions are an estimate, not a measurement; the ECDSA part has the widest range.

Two sources disagree on the flash use of board B: hil/firmware/SafetyNode/ssc_ota.h comment says about 26 %; hil/build/fw_b/SafetyNode.ino.bin says 78.7 % (1031920 bytes of 1310720). This design uses the measured build output (78.7 %); the ssc_ota.h comment is stale and should be corrected.

The scope baseline 'bus load at most the observed 1.11 %' cannot be a ceiling for programming traffic: moving the image at that share takes 61.01 min; at a proposed 10 % cap it takes 6.77 min (406.3 s). Owner decision: the cap for programming traffic, and that the baseline applies to the running traffic only.

ECDSA P-256 verify takes an estimated 100 to 500 ms in software: run inline in the 10 ms control loop it would miss 10 to 50 cycles. It must run in its own task with a watchdog feed, only while no scenario runs (the existing BUSY rule). Unmeasured.

The supply floor of the precondition and the sag/brown-out tests rest on a brown-out threshold that is UNMEASURED (placeholders 9.0 V / 9.5 V in the plant model). The floor must be set above the measured recovery threshold with a margin; measure it on the bench (gap G-N12-tests) before any claim.

All-or-nothing activation needs a board to roll back AFTER it committed. Today a committed image is final (anti-downgrade refuses the old version). The design therefore adds a commit-pending state that keeps the old slot until the whole campaign is confirmed, and an authorised campaign rollback that anti-downgrade must allow. Both change the existing, proven update path of board B (REL-01..12 must pass again).
The flash-side timing (erase 45 ms per sector, write 100 KiB/s) and the code-size figures are estimates, not measurements; the verdicts that depend on them are marked as estimates.

SecurityAccess (0x27) needs a seed/key scheme. Where the shared secret lives is an owner decision: a key on the gateway is a second secret next to the image-signing key (which must stay off the boards). Until decided the step is specified but not designed.

Board A is both the gateway and the owner of the power-cut relay. If the gateway resets in the middle of a campaign the targets must time out the programming session and keep the running slot; a campaign interrupted after activation must be completed or rolled back at the next start (state kept on the PC manifest).
Flash time at the proposed 10 % bus share is computed as 406.3 s. The ISO-TP flow-control and separation-time settings are not defined (G-N20-software missing), so the real time may differ.

findings.text: No firmware reads the divider: there is no analogRead / ADC call in hil/firmware or hil/SafeStopCore/src, and no DID or status op returns a supply voltage measured on board B. VEH_SupplyState (0x302) is DECODED by ssc_precond from the CAN bus; its source in this pilot is the plant model on the PC. The divider is therefore wiring that nothing reads yet: a firmware follow-up (read the ADC, expose it read-only) is needed before it can be calibrated or used by the precondition.
findings.basis: code scan of hil/ for ADC calls

findings.text: The thresholds of owner decision OD-5 (3700 mV floor, 3000 mV abort) are on board B's own 5 V rail, but board B does not run from that rail directly: a regulator makes its 3V3, and that regulator and its dropout are not recorded in the repo (config/hardware.json). A typical linear regulator on a dev board (dropout about 1 V; VERIFY on the real board) stops holding 3.3 V when the rail falls to about 4.3 V, and the chip then browns out and resets. If board B resets above the floor, the floor and the abort can never be seen by its own firmware, and the abort is unreachable. Measure the rail voltage at which board B resets and comes back (guide 'measurements', M1) before relying on the thresholds; this stage does not change them.

The divider parts are not in the approved plan: the approved BOM has one generic proposed line, and the values, filter capacitor, series resistor and clamp diodes are new. Owner decision D-02 allows a divider (about 10 INR); adding these specific lines means re-running the plan and re-approving it. This stage does not touch the plan.

Common ground: the divider's ground is board B's ground, which reaches the PC through the data-only USB lead (GND). A supply whose negative is earthed would tie its ground to the PC. Use the floating pack or an isolated bench supply.

The relay module's switching from a 3.3 V GPIO is UNCONFIRMED. The pin current is inside the limit under both quoted trigger currents, so no driver is needed to protect the pin; whether the relay fully switches is measured at step R3 of the relay guide, with a fallback NPN driver prepared.

The relay input pin floats while board A resets or boots. If the module has no pull-down, the relay could chatter and cut board B's supply at the wrong moment. A 10 kohm pull-down at IN is recommended; step R5 of the relay guide measures it.
Board B's supply current (idle, scenario, Wi-Fi transmitting) and the relay contact rating are UNKNOWN. The 2 A adapter rating is known. No budget verdict is given until they are measured.
Relay may not switch reliably from a 3.3 V GPIO; this is unconfirmed until measured in guide step R3.
Relay IN floats while board A resets or boots. Without a module pull-down, the relay could actuate and cut board B's power unexpectedly.
Board B supply current and relay contact rating are unknown, so the relay may be under-rated for the load.
No firmware reads the divider, so the OD-5 thresholds (3700 mV floor, 3000 mV abort) are not yet enforced or verified on hardware.

computations.title: Divider ratio and resistor choice
computations.method: Search the E96 (1 %) and E24 (5 %) series for R1, R2 with R1 + R2 in 20 to 200 kohm. Keep the pairs whose worst-case high ratio puts the top of the supply range under headroom x the ADC limit and whose worst-case source impedance is under the guidance; take the one with the highest worst-case LOW ratio.
steps: top of range 5.5 V, ADC design limit 2.45 V (assumption A-ADC-LIMIT), headroom 0.95 -> k_hi x 5.5 V <= 2.328 V
chosen E96 1 %: R1 = 19100 ohm, R2 = 13700 ohm, 28674 pairs tried
pin voltage at 5.5 V: nominal 2.297 V, worst 2.324 V; at 2.5 V: worst 1.032 V

computations.title: Worst-case supply-voltage error at the abort threshold
computations.method: Sum of the worst-case terms, referred to the supply: resistor ratio, ADC leakage x source impedance, ADC error (uncalibrated, or calibrated against a multimeter), half an LSB.
steps: at 3.00 V: ratio 35 mV + leakage 20 mV + ADC (uncalibrated, A-ADC-ERR) 121 mV + half LSB 0.7 mV = 176 mV
after a two-point calibration: ADC residual (A-ADC-CAL) 36 mV + half LSB = 37 mV
required: <= abort threshold - recovery threshold = 500 mV -> uncalibrated OK, calibrated OK

computations.title: RC filter at the ADC pin and sampling
computations.method: tau = (R1 || R2) x C; time to settle to 1 LSB after the supply step of the transient run = tau x ln(step at the pin / LSB).
steps: tau = 7978 ohm x 100 nF = 0.798 ms; corner 199 Hz
settling to 1 LSB (0.598 mV) after a 3 V step (1.253 V at the pin): 6.10 ms
source impedance with the 1 kohm series resistor: 9058 ohm against the 10000 ohm guidance

computations.title: Divider dissipation
steps: at 6 V: I = 0.168 mA, P(R1) = 0.54 mW, P(R2) = 0.39 mW against 250 mW parts (limit: half the rating)

computations.title: Relay input drive for a quoted trigger current of 5.0 mA
computations.method: GPIO -> series R -> optocoupler LED; R set so the module draws the quoted current at 5 V; evaluated at 3.3 V.
steps: R = (5.0 V - 1.2 V) / 5.0 mA = 760 ohm (the module's series resistance if it quotes 5.0 mA at 5 V)
I at 3.3 V = (3.3 - 1.2) / 760 = 2.76 mA; at VOH min 2.64 V: 1.89 mA; pin limit 20 mA

computations.title: Relay input drive for a quoted trigger current of 20.0 mA
computations.method: GPIO -> series R -> optocoupler LED; R set so the module draws the quoted current at 5 V; evaluated at 3.3 V.
steps: R = (5.0 V - 1.2 V) / 20.0 mA = 190 ohm (the module's series resistance if it quotes 20.0 mA at 5 V)
I at 3.3 V = (3.3 - 1.2) / 190 = 11.05 mA; at VOH min 2.64 V: 7.58 mA; pin limit 20 mA

computations.title: Fallback low-side NPN driver (only if the 3.3 V switch test fails)
computations.method: Ib = Ic / hFE_min x overdrive; Rb from VOH_min.
steps: collector current to pull IN down: up to 20.0 mA (the larger quoted trigger current)
base current needed = Ic / hFE_min x overdrive = 20.0 mA / 100 x 10 = 2.00 mA
Rb <= (VOH_min 2.64 V - Vbe 0.7 V) / 2.00 mA = 970 ohm -> E24 value 910 ohm
base current at 3.3 V = (3.3 - 0.7) / 910 = 2.86 mA on the pin (limit 20 mA)

steps.title: Set the relay's trigger jumper to H (high-level trigger)
steps.action: Put the H/L jumper on H. High-level trigger plus the normally-closed contact means board B stays powered while board A boots, resets or hangs; B loses power only while A actively holds GPIO6 high.
steps.safety: Unpowered module.

expect.text: The jumper bridges the H pins (check the silkscreen of your module).

traps.text: A low-level-trigger setting would cut B's power whenever A reboots.

steps.model_tip: Jumper position is easy to miss: set it to H before any wiring. Wrong setting inverts the logic, so the relay is on when it should be off.

steps.title: Bench-test the relay alone from a 3.3 V pin (does it switch at 3.3 V?)

steps.safety: mA range is only ever used in series, never across a supply or a pin. Nothing is connected to COM, NO or NC except the meter's continuity probe. Remove the 3V3 wire before you leave the step.

expect.text: The relay clicks, COM-NC continuity opens, and the current into IN is at most 20 mA (the pin limit used in the electrical draft; the model predicts about 2.76 to 11.05 mA for the two quoted trigger currents). If the relay does not click, STOP: do not continue; use the fallback NPN driver of the electrical draft first.

traps.text: Never put board A's supply through the relay: A drives the relay and is the observer.

steps.title: Check that IN stays low while board A is in reset
steps.action: Plug board A in. Hold its RESET (EN) button and measure the voltage from relay IN to GND with the meter; release it and measure again once board A has booted.
steps.safety: Voltage range, probes only on IN and GND.

swd.text:
# Software design descriptions (SWD) for the T6 update-path modules

Status: **DRAFT, waiting for the owner's `swd_review` gate.** AI-assisted, synthetic, illustrative; no compliance claim.

One file per module, written before the code (stage 10, step 1). The independent unit and conformance tests were written
from these files plus the architecture draft, by a separate run that never saw the code.

Common rules for every module

- Sans-I/O C++17 in `hil/SafeStopCore/src/`, no heap, no Arduino calls, fixed-size buffers. Time is a `uint32_t` count of milliseconds
  given by the caller (`now_ms`); all time differences use unsigned subtraction (wrap-safe).
- Everything new sits behind flags that default OFF (`ssc_ota_cfg.h`). With all flags OFF the new `.cpp` files are empty and board B's
  proven update path (`hil/firmware/SafetyNode/ssc_ota.h`, REL-01..12) is unchanged.
- Provisional values (bus-share cap, supply floor, SecurityAccess scheme, CAN id proposals) are named constants in `ssc_ota_cfg.h`,
  each marked `PROVISIONAL: owner decision OD-n`. Tests read them through `ssc_cfg_get` (below) so a changed decision changes no test.
- Tags `[need Nxx]` name the need of the gap report (`tsp_work/requests/ota-production-style-2/plan/gap_report.json`); the same tag
  appears as a `// [need Nxx]` comment in the code and in the tests. `[req UPD-xx]` names a proposed requirement in `safety/proposed_upd.json`.
- **Test bridge:** the PC build adds a C API (file `ssc_host_prog.cpp`, only under `SSC_HOST_API`) in the DLL named by the environment
  variable `SSC_FW_DLL`. The tests drive it with `ctypes`. Each SWD lists the functions it needs under "Test bridge".

Modules

# SWD: ssc_commit (optional commit-pending state and authorised rollback)

Status: DRAFT (waits for `swd_review`). Owner decision OD-2 (2026-10-16): adopt, behind `SSC_COMMIT_MACHINE` (default OFF on the board). AI-assisted, synthetic, illustrative.

## 1. Responsibility
The campaign rule "all boards of a campaign roll back together" (owner decision D-01b) needs a board to go back to its previous image AFTER its own trial
passed, until the whole campaign is confirmed. Today a committed image is final and anti-downgrade refuses the old version. This module is the small state
machine that says which transitions are legal and when going back is authorised. It is a **separate optional module, not wired into the default path of
board B**: the proven path (`ssc_ota.h`) never calls it. Only the campaign adapter (`ssc_ota_adapter`, flags on) uses it. [need N08] [req UPD-07]
Architecture risk R6 is accepted by the owner's OD-2 (adopt); the rollback on the real board stays untested on hardware until the flag is turned on and REL-01..12 are re-run.

## 2. Interface (C++, namespace `ssc::commit`)
```
enum State : uint8_t { IDLE = 0, STAGED = 1, TRIAL = 2, COMMIT_PENDING = 3, CONFIRMED = 4, ROLLED_BACK = 5 };
enum Event : uint8_t { STAGE = 1, ACTIVATE = 2, TRIAL_PASSED = 3, CONFIRM = 4, ROLLBACK = 5, ABORT = 6, CLEAR = 7 };
class Machine {
  void init();
  int  apply(Event e);                         // the new State (>= 0) if legal; -1 if illegal (state unchanged)
  State state() const;
  void set_previous_minor(int minor);          // minor version of the image that ROLLBACK returns to (recorded at ACTIVATE time by the caller)
  bool downgrade_allowed(int candidate_minor, int running_minor) const;
};
```

## 3. Transition table (any pair not listed is illegal and changes nothing)
| From | Event | To |
|---|---|---|
| IDLE | STAGE | STAGED |
| STAGED | ACTIVATE | TRIAL |
| STAGED | ABORT | IDLE |
| TRIAL | TRIAL_PASSED | COMMIT_PENDING |
| TRIAL | ROLLBACK | ROLLED_BACK |
| COMMIT_PENDING | CONFIRM | CONFIRMED |
| COMMIT_PENDING | ROLLBACK | ROLLED_BACK |
| CONFIRMED, ROLLED_BACK, IDLE | CLEAR | IDLE |
`CONFIRMED` is final for rollback: after it, `ROLLBACK` is illegal (the old slot may be released).
`downgrade_allowed(candidate, running)`: true when `candidate > running` (an ordinary update), and also true when the state is `TRIAL` or `COMMIT_PENDING` and
`candidate == previous minor` (the authorised campaign rollback). In every other state a candidate that is not newer is refused (the anti-downgrade rule is kept).

## 4. States and persistence
Six states (above). Persistence across a reset is the caller's job (the target keeps the state in NVS next to the existing trial record); the module itself is RAM only.

## 5. Timing and resources
Constant time, a few bytes, no heap.

## 6. Requirement / need mapping
- [need N08] stated activation rule: stage all, activate all, trial, commit-pending, confirm together; rollback until confirmed.
- [req UPD-07] A board of a campaign can return to its previous image until the campaign is confirmed; after confirmation it cannot.

# SWD: ssc_ecdsa (ECDSA P-256 verify)

Status: DRAFT (waits for `swd_review`). AI-assisted, synthetic, illustrative.

## 1. Responsibility
Verify an ECDSA signature over the NIST P-256 curve (secp256r1) on a 32-byte digest, with the public key only (FIPS 186-4 verify, SEC 1 point
rules). Portable code with a HAL hook, so a target build can later route the call to mbedTLS (`mbedtls_ecdsa_verify`) without changing callers.
The private key never exists on a board. [need N05]

## 2. Interface (C++, namespace `ssc::ecdsa`)
```
typedef bool (*VerifyHook)(const uint8_t pub[64], const uint8_t hash[32], const uint8_t sig[64]);
void set_hook(VerifyHook h);                                         // null = use the portable code (default)
bool pub_valid(const uint8_t pub[64]);                               // X || Y, big-endian, on the curve, coordinates < p, not the point at infinity
bool verify(const uint8_t pub[64], const uint8_t hash[32], const uint8_t sig[64]);   // sig = r || s, each 32 bytes big-endian
bool pub_from_priv(const uint8_t priv[32], uint8_t pub[64]);         // test/tool helper: k*G; false for k = 0 or k >= n
```
`verify` returns true only for a valid signature. It returns false (never crashes, never reads outside the three arrays) for: r = 0, s = 0, r >= n, s >= n,
a public key that fails `pub_valid` (not on the curve, a coordinate >= p, (0,0)), a digest or signature that does not match, and the degenerate result
(u1*G + u2*Q is the point at infinity). `s` is **not** required to be in the lower half: both (r, s) and (r, n-s) verify. When a hook is set, `verify` returns
exactly what the hook returns, after the portable range checks of the signature and key have passed (the hook is never called with r/s out of range or a bad key).
`verify` uses `digest` as the leftmost 256 bits (the digest is exactly 32 bytes; it is reduced modulo n as an integer, per FIPS 186-4).

## 3. The signed message of an image (used by `ssc_ota_adapter`, not by this module)
`digest = SHA-256( "SSA1" || sha256(image)[32] || size_u32_LE || version_ascii )`. The magic keeps a signature of one purpose from verifying as another.

## 4. States
None (pure function). The hook pointer is the only state.

## 5. Timing, resources, honest limits
- No heap. Stack: a few hundred bytes of 256-bit numbers. Estimated 100..500 ms on the ESP32-S3 in portable code (architecture risk R4: **unmeasured**); it
  must run outside the 10 ms control loop and only while no scenario runs (the existing BUSY rule).
- **Constant time is NOT claimed.** The verify handles public data only (public key, digest, signature), so timing does not leak a secret. `pub_from_priv`
  handles a private scalar and is a test/tool helper that must not be linked into a product image for use with real keys; it is compiled out of target builds.
- Not a FIPS-validated implementation; checked against OpenSSL (through the Python `cryptography` package) and public NIST/RFC 6979 vectors.

## 6. Requirement / need mapping
- [need N05] verify with a public key on the board; private key off the boards.
- [req UPD-02] the update is accepted only when the asymmetric signature verifies.

## 7. Test bridge (C ABI)
```
int  ssc_ecdsa_verify(const uint8_t pub[64], const uint8_t hash[32], const uint8_t sig[64]);   // 1 valid, 0 invalid
int  ssc_ecdsa_pub_valid(const uint8_t pub[64]);                                               // 1 / 0
int  ssc_ecdsa_pub_from_priv(const uint8_t priv[32], uint8_t pub[64]);                         // 1 ok, 0 failed
void ssc_ecdsa_test_hook(int mode, int *calls);   // 0: no hook; 1: a hook that returns true; 2: a hook that returns false. *calls (may be null) points at a counter the hook increments
```
References: Python `cryptography` (OpenSSL) for key generation, signing and verification; the public RFC 6979 A.2.5 (P-256, SHA-256, message "sample")
vector, itself validated against OpenSSL by the test before it is used.

## 3. Sequence (per phase, boards are handled one after the other; the bus carries one request at a time)
| Phase (State) | For every board in order | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| PRECHECK | local `precond::check_start` with the gateway's own `SupplyMonitor` (fed by 0x302 frames). `set_bench_idle(false)` (a scenario runs on the bench) refuses with BUSY. While no fresh frame has been seen the verdict waits up to `SUPPLY_STALE_MS` after `start` (the first frame may still be on its way); after that SUPPLY_UNKNOWN is final; a version that is not newer than `old_ver` (minor, as the OTA machine) is refused too. Nothing is sent. | `R_REFUSED`, `refusal()` = the Result code (a version refusal uses code 6), no frame sent |
| STAGING | 0x10 0x02 -> 0x27 0x01 (seed) -> 0x27 0x02 (key from this board's secret, `Io::seca_secret`; no secret -> the step fails, NRC 0x33, no key is sent) -> 0x31 0x01 FF02 manifest -> 0x31 0x01 FF00 erase -> 0x34 -> 0x36 blocks of `MAX_BLOCK_LEN - 2` data bytes (the last shorter) -> 0x37 -> 0x31 0x01 FF01 verify. Block counter starts at 1. | before ACTIVATING nothing is activated: ABORT (below) -> `R_ABORTED` |
| STAGED | all boards verified: this is the barrier. No board is activated before every board reported FF01 positive. | |
| ACTIVATING | 0x31 0x01 0200 on every board, then 0x11 0x01 on every board. | rollback of every board already activated (below) -> `R_ROLLED_BACK` |
| TRIAL | each board, until `TRIAL_WAIT_MS`: wait for it to answer again after the reset (0x10 0x02 retried every 200 ms), 0x27 as above, 0x22 F195 equals `new_ver`, 0x22 F1A0 equals commit state TRIAL (2) or COMMIT_PENDING (3). | rollback of every board |
| COMMITTING | 0x31 0x01 0201 on every board. | rollback of every board (including boards already COMMIT_PENDING: authorised rollback) |
| CONFIRMING | 0x31 0x01 0202 on every board; reached only when **every** board is COMMIT_PENDING. | before the first confirm succeeded: rollback of every board; after at least one board confirmed: `R_PARTIAL_CONFIRM` (cannot go back for the confirmed ones; reported, not hidden) |
| ROLLING_BACK | per board that was activated (or whose activation was sent): 0x10 0x02 -> 0x27 -> 0x31 0x01 0203 -> 0x11 0x01 -> wait -> 0x22 F195 equals `old_ver`. A board that answers NRC 0x24 to 0203 and reports `old_ver` counts as returned (it rolled itself back). | a board that never reports `old_ver`: `R_ROLLBACK_INCOMPLETE` (its own trial logic returns it at the next reset) |
| ABORT (pre-activation failure) | 0x10 0x01 on every board that has a session (the target drops the half-written image). Boards that never answered (timeout or transport error) are skipped. | |

(In the C++ source the enumerators are named `RS_*`, because `R_OK` is a macro of <unistd.h>.) `R_OK` = every board confirmed. `R_ABORTED`/`R_REFUSED`: nothing was activated, running images untouched. `R_ROLLED_BACK`: every board reports its old version.
`fail_board()`, `fail_step()`, `last_nrc()` describe the first failure (NRC 0 when the cause was a timeout or a transport error).

**Request engine:** one outstanding request per board. A response is matched by the service id (`SID+0x40`, or `7F SID nrc`). NRC 0x78 extends the wait to `P2_STAR_MS`
from that moment (any number of 0x78). Ordinary wait `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`. A timeout is a failure of the step, except TransferData which is sent again with the **same**
block counter up to `BLOCK_RETRIES` times before it fails. Any other NRC is a failure of the step. An ISO-TP error on the sending side is a failure of the step.
**Keep-alive:** while any board holds a session, the gateway sends the functional TesterPresent `3E 80` (single frame, id 0x7DF) every 2000 ms.
**Pacing:** the target's flow control sets STmin (`STMIN_MS`, bus-share cap `BUS_SHARE_CAP_PERCENT`, OD-1) and block size; the gateway never sends a CF earlier (ISO-TP rules of `ssc_isotp`).
**Status frame** (id 0x303, DLC 8, proposed): `[state, board_index (the board being worked on or the failed board), progress_pct (bytes sent over all sizes, 0..100), last_nrc, refusal, images_total, images_done (boards verified), alive]`.

**Records (N04):** the campaign result, per-board steps and the first failure are what the PC writes into the run manifest as the per-update record (`fleet/campaign.py`).

## 4. States
Campaign: the table above. Per board: `Step` (current or last step), booleans activated / reset sent / has session / confirmed / returned.

## 5. Timing and resources
Fixed arrays for 4 boards: 4 ISO-TP endpoints with 1 KiB receive buffers for the small UDS answers (responses are < 16 bytes; a 64-byte buffer each is enough), one 1 KiB block buffer. No heap. Work per call to `poll`: constant.
A 1 MiB image at STmin 3 ms is about 440 s of bus time (architecture C3 gave 406 s at the 10 % cap).

## 1. Responsibility
Carry a message of 1..4095 bytes over classic CAN frames of at most 8 bytes: single frame (SF), first frame (FF), consecutive frames (CF), flow
control (FC) with block size and separation time, timeouts, error codes. Fixes the "single frame only" limit recorded in T1 (`ssc_uds.h`).
Used on both sides: the UDS server (board B) and the gateway client (board A). [need N20] [need N07] [need N15]

## 2. Interface (C++, namespace `ssc::isotp`)

                     E_UNEXP_PDU=8, E_WFT_OVRN=9, E_BUFFER_OVFL=10, E_BAD_FRAME=11 };

                uint8_t stmin;        // STmin byte sent in our FC

                uint16_t n_bs_ms, n_cr_ms, n_as_ms, n_ar_ms;    // 1000 each by default
                uint8_t fc_wait_max; };         // FC.WAIT frames tolerated per block (default 10)
class Endpoint {
  typedef bool (*TxFrame)(void *ctx, const uint8_t *d, uint8_t n);               // false = the bus did not take the frame
  typedef void (*OnMessage)(void *ctx, const uint8_t *d, uint16_t n);            // d valid only during the call
  typedef void (*OnError)(void *ctx, Err e, bool tx_side);
  void init(const Config &c, uint8_t *rx_buf, uint16_t rx_cap, TxFrame, OnMessage, OnError, void *ctx);
  Err  send(const uint8_t *d, uint16_t n, uint32_t now_ms);
  void on_frame(const uint8_t *d, uint8_t n, uint32_t now_ms);

};

## 3. Frame layout (classic CAN, DLC 8)
| Frame | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| SF | `0x0L d...` | L = 1..7 data bytes |
| FF | `0x1H LL d0..d5` | total length DL = (H<<8)\|LL, 8..4095, 6 data bytes |
| CF | `0x2S d...` | S = sequence number, first CF = 1, after 15 comes 0; up to 7 data bytes |
| FC | `0x3F BS ST` | F: 0 CTS, 1 WAIT, 2 OVFLW; BS block size; ST separation time |

Sent frames are padded to 8 bytes with `pad_byte` when `pad` is true; with `pad` false the frame has only the bytes it needs (SF: 1+L,
FF: 8, CF: 1+data, FC: 3). Received frames are never required to be padded.

STmin byte: 0x00..0x7F = that many milliseconds; 0xF1..0xF9 = 100..900 microseconds, **treated as 0 ms** (the time base is whole milliseconds);
every other value is reserved and is treated as 127 ms.

## 4. Behaviour
**Send** `send(d, n, now)`:
- `n == 0` or `n > 4095` -> `E_BAD_LEN`; a message still being sent -> `E_BUSY`; neither changes any state.
- `n <= 7`: one SF. If `TxFrame` returns false -> `E_TX_FAIL`, nothing else changes. Done, `tx_busy()` stays false.
- `n >= 8`: send the FF; if `TxFrame` returns false -> `E_TX_FAIL` and the message is dropped. Otherwise the sender is *waiting for FC*; the
  N_Bs timer starts at `now`.
- On a FC with flow status CTS (`BS`, `ST` decoded as above, FC shorter than 3 bytes is ignored with `E_BAD_FRAME` reported on the sending side): the sender sends CFs.
  BS = 0 means the rest of the message with no further FC; otherwise BS CFs and then wait for the next FC (N_Bs restarts when the block ends).
- A FC with WAIT: the N_Bs timer restarts and a counter increments; when the counter exceeds `fc_wait_max` -> abort with `E_WFT_OVRN` (tx).
  The counter resets on every CTS.
- A FC with OVFLW -> abort with `E_BUFFER_OVFL` (tx). Any other flow status -> abort with `E_INVALID_FS` (tx).
- A FC while the sender is not waiting for one is ignored (no error).
- CFs are sent **only from `poll`**. The first CF of a block is due `STmin` ms after the FC that opened the block; every next CF is due
  `STmin` ms after the previous CF. `poll` sends every CF that is due at `now` (so with STmin 0 a whole block goes out in one `poll`),
  stops at the first CF that `TxFrame` refuses (it is retried at the next `poll`), and aborts with `E_TX_FAIL` (tx) when refusals have
  lasted `n_as_ms` without a single success. Sequence numbers start at 1 and wrap 15 -> 0.
- N_Bs timeout: waiting for FC for `n_bs_ms` or longer (measured in `poll`) -> abort with `E_TIMEOUT_BS` (tx).

**Receive** `on_frame(d, n, now)`: the PCI type is the high nibble of `d[0]`. Types other than 0..3 are ignored (no error). `n == 0` is ignored.
- SF: length L = low nibble. `L == 0`, `L > 7` or `n < 1 + L` -> report `E_BAD_FRAME` (rx), nothing else changes. Otherwise, if a reception was in progress
  report `E_UNEXP_PDU` (rx) and discard it; then deliver the message at once through `OnMessage`.
- FF: `n` must be 8 and DL >= 8, else report `E_BAD_FRAME` (rx), nothing else changes. Otherwise, if a reception was in progress report `E_UNEXP_PDU` and discard it.
  If DL > `rx_cap`: send FC with OVFLW (BS 0, ST 0) and report `E_BUFFER_OVFL` (rx); no reception starts. Otherwise store the 6 bytes, send FC CTS carrying
  `Config.block_size` and `Config.stmin`, expect SN 1, start the N_Cr timer.
- CF: when no reception is in progress it is ignored. SN different from the expected one -> abort the reception with `E_WRONG_SN` (rx). Missing data bytes
  (the frame is shorter than `1 + min(7, remaining)`) -> abort with `E_BAD_FRAME` (rx). Otherwise store `min(7, remaining)` bytes (padding is dropped) and restart N_Cr.
  When the message is complete, the reception ends first, then `OnMessage` is called (it may call `send`). When `block_size > 0`, after `block_size` CFs of a block that
  did not complete the message, send FC CTS again.
- N_Cr timeout: no CF for `n_cr_ms` or longer (measured in `poll`) -> abort with `E_TIMEOUT_CR` (rx). A FC that `TxFrame` refused is retried at every `poll`;
  refusals lasting `n_ar_ms` abort the reception with `E_TX_FAIL` (rx).
- After an abort the endpoint side is idle; the next frame is processed as a fresh one. Reception and sending are independent state machines
  (a node can answer while a request is still being received only after the request completed, but the machines do not block each other).

## 5. Timing and resources
Per frame: constant work, no loops longer than 7 bytes. RAM: the caller's receive buffer plus about 40 bytes of state. Bus load is set by
`STmin` = `STMIN_MS` of `ssc_ota_cfg.h` (3 ms at the provisional 10 % cap: [PROVISIONAL: owner decision OD-1]); one 1024-byte block is 1 FF + 146 CF
(+ 1 FC) = 148 frames.

## 6. Requirement / need mapping
- [need N20] segmentation, flow control, block size, separation time, timeouts, error codes.
- [need N07] used on the registered diagnostic ids only (0x7E2/0x7EA, 0x7E3/0x7EB, 0x7DF); the module itself is id-agnostic.
- [need N15] STmin from the bus-share cap keeps programming traffic under the cap.

## 7. Test bridge (C ABI)

# SWD: ssc_ota_adapter (UDS server -> OTA state machine)

Status: DRAFT (waits for `swd_review`). AI-assisted, synthetic, illustrative.

## 1. Responsibility
Implements `prog::Target` on top of the **existing, unchanged** OTA state machine of board B (`ssc_ota.h`: BEGIN / CHUNK / END messages, A/B slots, trial boot, rollback).
It adds, in front of that machine: the asymmetric manifest check (ECDSA P-256), an independent SHA-256 of the received image, the update precondition and
the optional commit-pending state (`ssc_commit`). With the flags off none of this exists and the legacy path is byte-for-byte as before. [need N05] [need N06] [need N16] [req UPD-02] [req UPD-08] [req UPD-09]

Two small ports isolate the hardware: on the board they call `ota::handle`, `esp_ota_set_boot_partition` and `ESP.restart`; on the PC they call the Python
`EmuBoard` (the host emulation of `ssc_ota.h`, held to the firmware by `tests/test_fleet.py`).
```
struct Ports {
  void *ctx;
  // one OTA message (payload of a 'U' frame: op, ...) in, the reply payload (op, status, extra...) out. Returns 0 if the machine answered.
  int  (*ota_msg)(void *ctx, const uint8_t *msg, uint16_t n, uint8_t *reply, uint8_t *reply_len);
  int  (*slot_rollback)(void *ctx);   // switch the boot slot back to the previous (kept) slot; 0 = done
  void (*reboot)(void *ctx);
  int  (*running_minor)(void *ctx);   // minor version of the running image, for the anti-downgrade check
  bool (*pre_inputs)(void *ctx, precond::Inputs *in);   // current supply / vehicle / idle inputs (false = unknown)
};
struct AdapterCfg { const uint8_t *pub; const uint8_t *hmac_key; uint16_t hmac_key_len; };   // pub = 64-byte public key; hmac_key = the legacy key the OTA END check uses
class Adapter { void init(const AdapterCfg &c, const Ports &p); prog::Target target(); ... };
```

## 2. Interface: the manifest (routine 0xFF02 payload) and the ports
`"SSA1" | size u32 LE | sha256[32] | ver_len u8 | version ascii (1..16 bytes) | signature r||s [64]` (length 4+4+32+1+ver_len+64 = 105 + ver_len).
Signature covers `digest = SHA-256("SSA1" || sha256 || size_u32_LE || version)` (see `ssc_ecdsa.md`). The PC signer is `fleet/asym.py`.

## 3. Target calls
| Call | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `precondition` | `Ports.pre_inputs` false -> `SUPPLY_UNKNOWN`; else `precond::check_start`. |
| `manifest(d, n)` | Reject (T_REJECT) when the length is inconsistent with `ver_len`, `ver_len` is 0 or > 16, size < 1024 or > 0x140000. The signature is verified (`ecdsa::verify` with `cfg.pub`): invalid -> T_SIGNATURE and the manifest is **not** stored (a later erase is refused). A version that is not newer than the running image (`commit::downgrade_allowed(candidate, running)`, minors as in `ssc_ota.h`) -> T_REJECT. Valid: stored, machine event STAGE is not yet applied. |
| `erase` | Requires a stored manifest else T_BAD_SEQ. Runs `precond::check_continue` first (refused -> T_REJECT). Sends OTA BEGIN built from the manifest (size, sha256, HMAC computed with `hmac_key` over `sha256 \| size_u32_LE \| version` exactly as `ssc_ota.h` expects, version); a status other than OK -> T_REJECT (BUSY, DOWNGRADE, BAD_SIZE) or T_FAIL (NO_SPACE). Starts a fresh SHA-256 of the image. |
| `begin(size)` | `size` must equal the manifest size else T_REJECT. |
| `write(offset, d, n)` | `offset` must equal the bytes written so far (else T_BAD_SEQ). Before every write `precond::check_continue` (supply below the abort floor, vehicle state, stale supply): refused -> T_FAIL and the update is aborted (the legacy machine is told nothing; its half-written inactive slot is simply never activated, REL-04 behaviour). Sends the bytes as OTA CHUNK messages of at most 200 bytes and updates the SHA-256. A CHUNK status other than OK -> T_FAIL. |
| `finish` | All manifest-size bytes received else T_BAD_SEQ. |
| `verify` | Finishes the SHA-256 and compares it with the manifest's: different -> T_SIGNATURE (the hash does not match what the signature covers). Equal -> machine event STAGE. |
| `activate` | Requires STAGED, else T_BAD_SEQ. Sends OTA END (legacy: re-hash, HMAC, boot-slot switch, TRIAL recorded); a status other than OK -> T_FAIL. On OK: event ACTIVATE (TRIAL), `set_previous_minor(running minor)`. The board does not reboot by itself; the server's 0x11 does (via `Ports.reboot` after OTA REBOOT). |
| `commit_pending` | machine event TRIAL_PASSED (illegal -> T_BAD_SEQ). |
| `confirm` | machine event CONFIRM (illegal -> T_BAD_SEQ). |
| `rollback` | machine event ROLLBACK (illegal -> T_BAD_SEQ); on legal: `Ports.slot_rollback` (T_FAIL when it returns non-zero). The 0x11 reset that follows boots the old image. |
| `reset` | `Ports.reboot`. When the machine is STAGED/TRIAL the reset first sends OTA REBOOT. |
| `abort` | Drops a staged or partly received image: machine ABORT/CLEAR, the stored manifest and hash. The legacy machine's own `abort_update` happens at its next BEGIN. |
| `update_state` | the machine state (0..5) for DID 0xF1A0. |

The legacy machine keeps its own 3 s trial self-commit; the commit machine of this adapter is the campaign's view on top of it, and authorised rollback uses the previous slot
that the OTA machine does not erase. Honest limit: on the real board this relies on the old slot still holding a valid image after the legacy commit and on `esp_ota_set_boot_partition` back to it;
that is **untested on hardware**. **OD-2 was decided by the owner on 2026-10-16: adopt.** It is switched by `AdapterCfg::commit_machine` (board flag `SSC_COMMIT_MACHINE`, default OFF until REL-01..12 are re-run on the board; the PC build mirrors the decision and is on). With it OFF: the routines 0x0201 / 0x0202 / 0x0203 are not offered (NRC 0x31), nothing is persisted or restored, the slot-switch rollback is compiled out of the glue, and **the adapter refuses at the manifest (NRC 0x31), before anything is erased or written**, with a second refusal at activation, so a board without the machine can never be switched to a new image by a campaign that could not then be rolled back. A campaign over several boards stays all-or-nothing: one such board stops all of them.

## 4. States
`ssc_commit` states plus: manifest stored (bool), bytes written, SHA-256 context, image-hash-checked (bool).

## 5. Timing and resources
`manifest`: one ECDSA verify (estimated 100..500 ms on the ESP32-S3, unmeasured) which the glue must run outside the control loop; `write` per block: a SHA-256 update and ceil(n/200) OTA messages. No heap; a 200-byte message buffer on the stack.

- [need N16] [req UPD-09] unverified code never runs: no activation without hash-match + signature; a failed or interrupted download leaves the running slot untouched.

- [need N08] the commit-pending machine (`ssc_commit`) gives the campaign its authorised rollback; adopted by the owner (OD-2) behind `SSC_COMMIT_MACHINE`; not part of the legacy REL-01..12 path.

- [req UPD-08] a version that is not newer is refused at the manifest, and again by the legacy BEGIN.

# SWD: ssc_precond (update precondition, supply monitor)

Status: DRAFT (waits for `swd_review`). AI-assisted, synthetic, illustrative.

## 1. Responsibility
Decide, from plain inputs, whether an update may start or continue: supply voltage high enough, vehicle parked, bench idle, supply information fresh.
Also decode the proposed CAN message `VEH_SupplyState` (0x302) into those inputs, with its small E2E protection. Used by the target (board B) and by
the gateway (board A). Thresholds come from `ssc_ota_cfg.h` (provisional, OD-5). [need N09] [need N12] [req UPD-05]

## 2. Interface (C++, namespace `ssc::precond`)
```
enum Vehicle : uint8_t { V_UNKNOWN = 0, V_PARKED = 1, V_IGNITION_ON = 2, V_DRIVING = 3 };
enum Result : uint8_t { OK = 0, SUPPLY_LOW = 1, SUPPLY_UNKNOWN = 2, NOT_PARKED = 3, BUSY = 4, VEHICLE_UNKNOWN = 5 };
struct Inputs { uint16_t supply_mv; uint32_t supply_age_ms; bool supply_valid; uint8_t vehicle_state; bool bench_idle; };
Result check_start(const Inputs &in);          // before the first request of an update
Result check_continue(const Inputs &in);       // while an update runs (abort floor, vehicle state, supply freshness)
class SupplyMonitor {
  void init();
  // returns 0 accepted, 1 wrong id/length, 2 CRC wrong, 3 counter not advanced (repeated or replayed frame)
  int  on_frame(uint16_t id, const uint8_t *d, uint8_t n, uint32_t now_ms);
  Inputs inputs(uint32_t now_ms, bool bench_idle) const;
};
void encode_supply_state(uint16_t supply_mv, uint8_t vehicle_state, uint8_t alive, uint8_t out[4]);
```

## 3. Rules
`check_start`, evaluated in this order, the first that applies wins:
1. `!bench_idle` -> `BUSY` (a scenario is running; the existing BUSY rule).
2. `vehicle_state == V_UNKNOWN` -> `VEHICLE_UNKNOWN`; `V_IGNITION_ON` or `V_DRIVING` (any other value too) -> `NOT_PARKED`.
3. `!supply_valid` or `supply_age_ms >= SUPPLY_STALE_MS` -> `SUPPLY_UNKNOWN` (unknown is a refusal, never a pass).
4. `supply_mv < SUPPLY_FLOOR_MV` -> `SUPPLY_LOW` (exactly at the floor passes).
5. otherwise `OK`.
`check_continue` is the same, except rule 4 uses `SUPPLY_ABORT_MV` (a running update tolerates a lower voltage than a start needs; below the abort floor it stops).

**VEH_SupplyState frame** (proposed id 0x302, DLC 4, every 100 ms) [PROPOSED, owner decision OD-4]:
byte 0 = supply_mv low byte, byte 1 = supply_mv high byte, byte 2 = vehicle_state, byte 3 = `(alive << 4) | crc4`, alive = 0..15 counter that increments by 1 (mod 16) per
frame. `crc4` = CRC-4 (polynomial x^4 + x + 1 = 0x3, initial value 0xF, no reflection, no final xor), computed bit by bit, most significant bit first, over
bytes 0, 1, 2 and then the 4 bits of `alive` (as the high nibble of a fourth byte, only its top 4 bits are processed). [PROVISIONAL: the E2E profile is "to be fixed in the interface requirement" in the architecture draft.]
`SupplyMonitor::on_frame`: id != 0x302 or `n != 4` -> 1; CRC mismatch -> 2; the first valid frame is accepted; afterwards the alive counter must equal the previous + 1 (mod 16), else 3 (a repeated
or skipped counter is not accepted and does not refresh the age; the counter of the rejected frame is NOT adopted). An accepted frame stores supply, vehicle state and its arrival time.
`inputs(now, idle)`: `supply_valid` false before any accepted frame; `supply_age_ms = now - arrival`.

## 4. States
`SupplyMonitor`: EMPTY (no frame yet) -> TRACKING. `check_*` are stateless.

## 5. Timing and resources
Constant time, a dozen bytes of state, no heap. The CAN message is 100 ms periodic, so freshness `SUPPLY_STALE_MS` = 500 ms means five missed frames. Thresholds are placeholders
(the board's brown-out threshold is unmeasured; architecture risk R5).

## 6. Requirement / need mapping
- [need N09] refuse below a floor; read vehicle state and supply. [req UPD-05]
- [need N12] supply sag during an update: `check_continue` stops it below `SUPPLY_ABORT_MV`. [req UPD-06]

1. Call the hook exactly `SAMPLES` times. A sample is *plausible* when `0 <= code <= ADC_FULL_SCALE_CODE`; a negative code (failed read) or a code above full scale is dropped.
   `samples` = the number of plausible samples (0..SAMPLES). `sum` = their sum.
2. If `samples < MIN_VALID`: result `status = OPEN`, `mv = 0`, `code_mean = 0`, and the three further steps are skipped.
3. `code_mean = (sum + samples/2) / samples` (integer division, rounds half up).
4. Nominal rail voltage, one rounded integer division on the whole sum (no intermediate rounding):
   `nominal_mv = (sum * ADC_FS_MV * (R1_OHM + R2_OHM) + D/2) / D` with `D = samples * ADC_FULL_SCALE_CODE * R2_OHM` (all unsigned 64-bit, division truncating).
5. Calibrated: `mv = (nominal_mv * gain + 8192) / 16384 + offset` (gain is Q14, `/` truncates toward zero on the non-negative product), then clamped to `0..65535`.
   With no calibration the neutral values are used (gain 16384, offset 0), so an uncalibrated reading is the nominal value.
6. Status, first rule that applies wins:
   - `code_mean <= OPEN_CODE_MAX` -> `OPEN` and `mv = 0` (flat at the bottom: divider open or pin shorted; also what Arduino's `analogRead` returns when its init failed);
   - `code_mean >= SAT_CODE_MIN` -> `SATURATED` (flat at full scale: the input is above the converter's range; `mv` is the computed value, a lower bound of the truth);
   - `cal_state != CAL_SET` -> `UNCALIBRATED` (`mv` is the nominal value);
   - otherwise `OK`.
   (`CAL_INVALID` counts as not set.) The reading carries `cal_state` as it is at the time of the read.

## 4. Calibration (runtime, per board, stored in NVS by the glue)
`calibrate(gain_q14, offset_mv, busy, allowed)`, first rule that applies wins, the state is changed only on `CAL_OK`:
1. `!allowed` -> `CAL_DENIED` (the caller does not hold the unlock, or the build does not offer the write: section 5).
2. `busy` -> `CAL_BUSY` (a scenario or an update is running).
3. `gain_q14 == 0 && offset_mv == 0` -> clear: neutral values, `CAL_NONE`, `CAL_OK`.
4. `gain_q14 < GAIN_MIN || gain_q14 > GAIN_MAX` -> `CAL_RANGE`; `offset_mv < -OFFSET_LIMIT_MV || offset_mv > OFFSET_LIMIT_MV` -> `CAL_RANGE` (the limits themselves are accepted).
5. otherwise store the values, `CAL_SET`, `CAL_OK`.

NVS record (6 bytes, built and read by `blob` / `load`): byte 0 = version 1; bytes 1-2 = gain, big endian; bytes 3-4 = offset as a big-endian two's-complement 16-bit value;
byte 5 = `crc8` over bytes 0..4. `blob` returns 6 and fills the record when the state is `CAL_SET`, else 0 (nothing to store). `load(blob, n)`: first the neutral values and
`CAL_NONE`; `n == 0` -> stay so; otherwise `CAL_INVALID` unless `n == 6`, version 1, the CRC matches and the gain and offset are inside the limits of rule 4 (a record of
all zeros is not valid) -> then the values are adopted and the state is `CAL_SET`. The glue calls `load` at boot and, after every `CAL_OK` write, stores `blob` (or erases the key when it returns 0).

A calibration is done with two multimeter readings (guide `supply-divider`): read the DID at two rail voltages, then
`gain = (m2 - m1) / (n2 - n1)`, `offset = m1 - gain * n1`, where `n` is the DID's mV on an uncalibrated board and `m` the multimeter.

## 5. Who may write the calibration
| Build | Calibration write `0x2E 0xF1A1` |
|---|---|
| `SSC_SUPPLY_ADC` OFF | not compiled |
| `SSC_SUPPLY_ADC=1`, programming server OFF, `SSC_SUPPLY_CAL` OFF (default) | **not offered**: the plain UDS responder answers `0x2E` with NRC 0x11 like any other unsupported service. A production-like build cannot be calibrated by accident. |
| `SSC_SUPPLY_ADC=1`, programming server OFF, `SSC_SUPPLY_CAL=1` | offered in the plain responder (no session, no unlock exist there); NRC 0x21 while busy |
| programming server ON (`SSC_UDS_PROGRAMMING`) | offered by the programming server **only in the programming session (0x10 02) and after SecurityAccess (0x27)**; `SSC_SUPPLY_CAL` is not consulted |
The read (DID `0xF1A1`) is available in every build that has `SSC_SUPPLY_ADC`, in every session, without unlock.
**Busy** = a scenario is running on the node, or an update is in progress (the OTA state machine receiving or staged, a download open or a deferred call pending in the programming server).

## 6. UDS (ISO 14229 roles; DID and rules are bench choices)
Both responders (the plain single-frame responder `ssc_uds.h` of board B and the programming server `ssc_uds_prog`) offer, when the node has a supply port installed:

**ReadDataByIdentifier `0x22 F1 A1`** -> `0x62 F1 A1 <mv hi> <mv lo> <state> <samples>` (4 data bytes, **single frame**: 3 + 4 = 7 bytes, no multi-frame needed).
`<state>` = `(cal_state << 4) | status`. `<samples>` = `Reading.samples`. A request of the wrong length -> NRC 0x13. A node with no supply port answers NRC 0x31 (unknown DID).
Example: 4210 mV, status OK (0), calibration set (1), 16 samples -> frame `07 62 F1 A1 10 72 10 10`.

**WriteDataByIdentifier `0x2E F1 A1 <gain hi> <gain lo> <offset hi> <offset lo>`** (7 bytes of UDS payload: still a single frame; offset is a two's-complement 16-bit value)
-> `0x6E F1 A1`. All-zero data clears the calibration. Checks in this order, first that applies wins:
1. the service is not offered by this build (section 5) -> NRC 0x11 (plain) — in the programming server, no port or no write callback -> NRC 0x11;
2. payload length != 7 -> NRC 0x13; DID != `0xF1A1` -> NRC 0x31;
3. programming server only: session is not the programming session -> NRC 0x7F; not unlocked -> NRC 0x33; update flow active -> NRC 0x21;
4. the calibration rules of section 4 with `allowed = true`: busy -> NRC 0x21, out of range -> NRC 0x31 (`nrc_of`).
A functional request (0x7DF) to `0x2E` is never answered. The write goes through the callback of the glue, which stores the record in NVS (a failed store answers NRC 0x72).

Calibration state in the answer: 0 none (neutral values, status UNCALIBRATED), 1 set, 2 a stored record was found but did not check out (neutral values, status UNCALIBRATED).

## 7. Precondition source (`ssc_precond`, behind `SSC_SUPPLY_SOURCE_ADC`; default CAN)
New in `ssc::precond`:
```
enum Result : uint8_t { OK=0, SUPPLY_LOW=1, SUPPLY_UNKNOWN=2, NOT_PARKED=3, BUSY=4, VEHICLE_UNKNOWN=5, ADC_NOT_OK=6, SOURCE_MISMATCH=7 };
enum Source : uint8_t { SRC_CAN = 0, SRC_ADC = 1 };
struct AdcInputs { bool present; uint8_t status; uint16_t mv; };      // status is a supply::Status; 0 = OK
Result check_start_src   (const Inputs &in, const AdcInputs &adc, Source src);
Result check_continue_src(const Inputs &in, const AdcInputs &adc, Source src);
```
`src == SRC_CAN`: **exactly** `check_start` / `check_continue` (the ADC inputs are ignored). Any other `src` value takes the ADC rules below (the stricter path).
`src == SRC_ADC`, first rule that applies wins (the floor is `SUPPLY_FLOOR_MV` for start, `SUPPLY_ABORT_MV` for continue):
1. `!in.bench_idle` -> `BUSY`.
2. `in.vehicle_state == V_UNKNOWN` -> `VEHICLE_UNKNOWN`; any other state but `V_PARKED` -> `NOT_PARKED`.
3. `!adc.present || adc.status != 0` -> `ADC_NOT_OK` (**fail-safe**: an unusable local reading refuses, even when the CAN value looks fine).
4. when the CAN value is available (`in.supply_valid && in.supply_age_ms < SUPPLY_STALE_MS`): if `|in.supply_mv - adc.mv| > SOURCE_TOL_MV` -> `SOURCE_MISMATCH` (a difference of exactly the tolerance passes).
   When the CAN value is not available (invalid or stale) the ADC alone decides: no refusal for that.
5. `adc.mv < floor` -> `SUPPLY_LOW` (exactly at the floor passes).
6. otherwise `OK`.
`SOURCE_TOL_MV` is PROVISIONAL (about three times the calibrated total error of the electrical draft; the uncalibrated error is 0.17..0.21 V, so an uncalibrated board is refused by rule 3 before it is ever compared).
The adapter (`ssc_ota_adapter`) carries a `supply_source` field in its configuration (default `SRC_CAN`) and an optional port `pre_adc`; with `SRC_CAN` its behaviour is the earlier one.
With `SRC_ADC`, if `pre_inputs` says unknown -> `SUPPLY_UNKNOWN` (as before); if the `pre_adc` port is missing or says unknown -> the ADC counts as not present -> `ADC_NOT_OK`.
`ADC_NOT_OK` and `SOURCE_MISMATCH` are answered to a DiagnosticSessionControl into the programming session as NRC 0x22 (conditionsNotCorrect); only `SUPPLY_LOW` is NRC 0x93.

## 8. States
`Reader`: calibration state `CAL_NONE` / `CAL_SET` / `CAL_INVALID` as above; no other state (each `read` is independent). `check_*_src` are stateless.

## 9. Timing and resources
One reading is `SAMPLES` = 16 hook calls: on the target each is one `analogRead` (one-shot ADC1 conversion); the time per call is UNMEASURED (expected tens of microseconds, VERIFY on the board),
so a reading blocks the loop for well under a millisecond. It runs only when a DID read or a precondition check asks for it, never from the 10 ms control loop. No heap, about 12 bytes of state, 64-bit integer arithmetic only (no float).
ADC1 only: the divider is on GPIO1 = ADC1 channel 0 (`electrical.json` `pin_allocation` PIN-1); ADC2 is never used (it is not available while Wi-Fi is on).

## 10. Errors and hazards
- Uncalibrated divider values: the nominal conversion is only as good as the resistor tolerance (1 %) and the ADC's gain error (tens of mV at the pin per the draft); status `UNCALIBRATED` says so, and the ADC precondition source refuses until the board is calibrated.
- The reading is the voltage at the board's 5 V pin side of the divider. Whether board B's 3V3 regulator keeps the chip alive down to the OD-5 floor is a separate open question (`docs/F11_RECHECK.md`).
- A short sample window cannot reject a periodic disturbance; the 100 nF at the pin node (corner about 200 Hz) does that.

- [need N12] abort a running update below the abort floor: `check_continue_src`. [req UPD-06]

# SWD: ssc_uds_prog (UDS programming server)

Status: DRAFT (waits for `swd_review`). AI-assisted, synthetic, illustrative. Service ids and NRC roles follow ISO 14229 as the author knows
them; the routine ids (0xFF00..0xFF02, 0x0200..0x0203) are **OEM-specific bench choices**, not standard values. No conformance claim.

## 1. Responsibility
Server side (board B, flag `SSC_UDS_PROGRAMMING`) of the update sequence of the architecture draft: sessions, SecurityAccess, routines, request download,
transfer data, transfer exit, ECU reset, plus 0x3E and 0x22 (as the existing `ssc_uds.h`, which stays as it is for the default path). The server works on whole
UDS messages (after ISO-TP) and drives the flash/OTA side only through a small `Target` interface of function pointers, so the same server runs on the PC against a
scripted or an emulated target. [need N06] [need N17] [need N07] [req UPD-03] [req UPD-04] [req UPD-10]

## 2. Interface (C++, namespace `ssc::prog`)

## 3. Services (physical addressing unless noted)
Response = positive: `SID+0x40 ...`; negative: `7F SID NRC`. Every request refreshes the session timer. The sub-function high bit 0x80 (suppress positive response) is honoured **only** for
0x3E and 0x10 (the positive response is suppressed, negative responses are still sent); for every other service the sub-function is compared as it arrives, so 0x80 | sub is an unknown sub-function (NRC 0x12).

| SID | Service | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| 0x10 | DiagnosticSessionControl | length 2 else NRC 0x13. Sub (low 7 bits) 0x01 default, 0x02 programming, 0x03 extended; any other -> 0x12. To 0x02: `Target.precondition` != 0 -> NRC 0x93 when the code is 1 (SUPPLY_LOW), else 0x22. A change of session (a request for a different session than the active one) locks SecurityAccess, ends any download (calls `Target.abort` when a download or a staged-but-not-activated flow existed) and clears the flow flags; the same session again changes nothing. Positive: `50 sub 00 32 01 F4` (P2 50 ms, P2* 5000 ms). |
| 0x27 | SecurityAccess | only in the programming session, else NRC 0x7F. Sub 0x01 requestSeed, 0x02 sendKey, other -> 0x12. Length: seed request 2, key request 6, else 0x13. Seed: 4 bytes from `seed_source`, big-endian; if already unlocked the seed is `00 00 00 00`. During lockout -> NRC 0x37. Key: first 4 bytes of SHA-256(the node's own secret, `SECA_SECRET_MIN`..`SECA_SECRET_MAX` bytes, \|\| the 4 seed bytes); compared in constant time. **The secret comes from `set_secret_source` (the HAL reads it from NVS), never from the source.** A node with no secret, or one outside the length limits, answers requestSeed (and sendKey) with NRC 0x33: it fails closed and can never be programmed. Key without a seed requested in this session -> 0x24. Wrong key -> 0x35; the `SECA_MAX_ATTEMPTS`-th consecutive wrong key -> 0x36 and a lockout of `SECA_LOCKOUT_MS`; the seed is consumed by any key attempt. Right key -> unlocked, positive `67 02`. A good key resets the attempt counter. After a lockout ends the counter restarts at 0. Per-board secret, owner decision OD-3 (2026-10-16). |
| 0x31 | RoutineControl | sub must be 0x01 (start), else 0x12. Programming session (else 0x7F) and unlocked (else 0x33) for every routine. Length: 4 (FF00, FF01, 0200..0203) else 0x13; FF02 needs 4 + at least 1 data byte. Unknown routine id -> 0x31. Order rules (NRC 0x24): FF00 needs the manifest accepted; FF01 needs the transfer exited; 0200 needs a good FF01; FF02 and FF00 are refused with 0x24 while a download is open. 0201, 0202, 0203 have no server-side order rule (the Target's commit machine decides, T_BAD_SEQ -> 0x24). Routine -> Target: FF00 erase (clears download/verify flags), FF01 verify, FF02 manifest(data), 0200 activate (clears the flow flags), 0201 commit_pending, 0202 confirm, 0203 rollback. Positive: `71 01 rid_hi rid_lo 00`. |
| 0x34 | RequestDownload | programming session else 0x7F, unlocked else 0x33. Length must be 11, `dataFormatIdentifier` = 0x00 and `addressAndLengthFormatIdentifier` = 0x44, address (4 bytes BE) = 0, else NRC 0x31 (any deviation of length or format, also size 0). Needs the erase done (else 0x24) and no download already open (else 0x24). `Target.begin(size)` (it may answer T_PENDING). Positive: `74 20 04 00` (length format 0x20, max block length 1024 = `MAX_BLOCK_LEN` big-endian). |
| 0x36 | TransferData | programming session else 0x7F, unlocked else 0x33, a download open else 0x24. Length >= 3 else 0x13, <= `MAX_BLOCK_LEN` else 0x13. Block counter starts at 1 and wraps 0xFF -> 0x00. A counter equal to the last accepted one is a repeated block: positive response, nothing written (idempotent resume). Any other wrong counter -> 0x73. Data longer than the bytes still expected -> 0x31. `Target.write(offset, data, n)`: T_OK counts the bytes; any other result -> 0x72. Positive: `76 counter`. |
| 0x37 | RequestTransferExit | programming session else 0x7F, unlocked else 0x33, download open else 0x24; length 1 else 0x13; fewer bytes received than announced -> 0x24 (the download stays open). `Target.finish()`. Positive: `77`. |
| 0x11 | ECUReset | length 2 else 0x13; sub 0x01 hardReset (others 0x12). Not allowed in the default session (NRC 0x7F). Positive `51 01`. `Target.reset` is called by `poll` once `RESET_DELAY_MS` have passed since the response, not before. |
| 0x3E | TesterPresent | length 2 else 0x13; sub 0x00 (0x80 suppresses the response) else 0x12. |
| 0x22 | ReadDataByIdentifier | length 3 else 0x13. DID 0xF195 version (up to 4 characters), 0xF18C serial (4 bytes), 0xF186 active session (1 byte: 1/2/3), 0xF1A0 update state (1 byte from `Target.update_state`); other DID -> 0x31. Positive `62 hi lo data`. |
| other | | NRC 0x11. |

**Functional addressing** (`functional == true`): only 0x3E, 0x10 and 0x22 are processed; any other SID is ignored (no response). A negative response with NRC 0x11, 0x12 or 0x31 is not sent (as in `ssc_uds.h`).
An empty request is ignored.

**Result mapping** (Target -> NRC) for 0x31/0x34/0x36/0x37: T_OK positive; T_REJECT 0x31; T_FAIL and T_SIGNATURE 0x72; T_BAD_SEQ 0x24; T_BUSY 0x21;
T_PENDING: send `7F SID 78` at once and remember the request; while a request is pending any new request except 0x3E gets NRC 0x21. `poll` calls `Target.poll_pending(fn)`; when it
returns something other than T_PENDING the final response (positive or the mapped NRC) is returned by that `poll`; if `P2_STAR_MS` pass since the request without a final result the
final response is NRC 0x72 and `Target.abort` is called.

**Session timer:** in the programming or extended session, `poll` returns to the default session when `S3_TIMEOUT_MS` have passed since the last request (same effects as a session change: lock, abort, flags cleared).

## 4. States
Session (default / programming / extended); locked / unlocked / lockout; flow flags manifest-ok -> erased -> download-open -> exited -> verified; pending request; pending reset.
Power-on state: default session, locked, no flags, attempt counter 0. A reset (power cycle) clears the lockout: **honest limit**, the counter is RAM only.

## 5. Timing and resources
No heap; the largest buffer is the caller's request/response buffer (1024 + a few bytes). `request` does constant work plus the `Target` call. A good block costs one `Target.write`.

(namespace `seca`, one blob per slot). The construction (first 4 bytes of SHA-256(secret || seed)) is unchanged, so only the source of the secret changed.

```
typedef uint8_t (*SecretFn)(void *ctx, uint8_t *out);   // writes the secret into out[SECA_SECRET_MAX], returns its length, 0 = none
void Server::set_secret_source(SecretFn, void *ctx);    // call after init(); without one SecurityAccess is refused (NRC 0x33)
void seca_key(const uint8_t *secret, uint8_t len, const uint8_t seed[4], uint8_t key[4]);
```

Provisioning is a separate small module, `ssc_seca_store` (sans-I/O, storage behind four function pointers), driven by the bench-link message `'Q'` (USB only, never over CAN):

| 'Q' payload (PC -> board) | Meaning | Reply `'q'` payload `[op, status, extra...]` |
|---|---|---|
| `01 slot len secret[len]` | SET: only into an empty slot; `len` 16..40 | status 0 OK, 1 BAD_MESSAGE, 2 BAD_LENGTH, 3 NO_STORE, 4 BUSY, 5 EXISTS, 6 BAD_SLOT |
| `02 slot` | CLEAR (`slot` 255 = all) | as above |
| `03` | INFO | per slot `provisioned:u8 len:u8 fingerprint:4` (fingerprint = first 4 bytes of SHA-256("ssc-seca-fp" \|\| secret)); **the secret is never sent back** |

Rules: SET and CLEAR are refused with BUSY while a scenario, an update or a campaign is running (INFO is never refused); a filled slot is never overwritten (CLEAR first);
a target board has 1 slot, the gateway 4 (one per target board index: the secret it presents to that board). Order of checks in SET: message shape, slot, length, busy, exists, store.

Gateway: `Io::seca_secret(ctx, board, out)` gives the secret of board `board`; with none (or outside the limits) that board's `ST_SEC_KEY` step fails with NRC 0x33 and **no key is ever sent**.

Honest limits: no flash encryption is enabled (the agent never does): anyone with physical access to a board can read its secret out of the flash. Fine for a bench, not for a vehicle.
The lockout counter is RAM only. The 4-byte key stays; the lockout (3 attempts, 10 s) is what limits guessing.

Test bridge additions: `ssc_ut_set_secret(h, bytes, n)`, `ssc_sim_set_secret(h, board, which, bytes, n)` (which 0 = the board, 1 = the gateway's copy, 2 = both; n = 0 = none),
`ssc_cfg_secret` (a random 32-hex-character test secret made when the DLL is first used, new for every process), and `ssc_sq_new / ssc_sq_handle / ssc_sq_fail / ssc_sq_secret / ssc_sq_free / ssc_sq_fingerprint`
(the `'Q'` handler over an in-memory store).
